records.context: the Gaussian blur before the maxima are found, in pixels. This is separate from the image enhancement chain's denoise, which has already run by the time a detector sees the image: the blur that gives one object one centre is usually much stronger than the blur wanted for measuring the object's edge, and the propagation measures the edge on the same blurred image. Leave the chain's denoise off unless the microscope field of view is genuinely noisy, or the two blurs compound.

records.context: Found through ``findChildren`` rather than by walking the menu bar's actions and calling ``QAction.menu()``. That reading is the obvious one and it does not survive on PySide6 6.11: the QMenu wrapper it returns is only valid while the QAction wrapper it came off is alive, so the menu went stale the moment this function returned — "Internal C++ object (PySide6.QtWidgets.QMenu) already deleted" on the very next line — and keeping the owners alive as attributes segfaulted during the next event dispatch instead. ``findChildren`` hands back children the menu bar owns in C++, which stay valid for as long as the window does.

records.source: Found through ``findChildren`` rather than by walking the menu bar's actions and calling ``QAction.menu()``. records.translation: Fundið með ``findChildren`` en ekki með því að fara yfir aðgerðir valmyndastikunnar og kalla á ``QAction.menu()``. records.source: Sizes that do not pass through a setter are not rescaled live: text and shapes a widget paints itself at fixed pixel coordinates, pixmaps a widget scales to a number it computed, ``setFont`` with an explicit size, ``move``/``setGeometry`` positions, header section sizes, a Python ``sizeHint`` override that returns a constant, the Fusion style's own metrics that the theme sheet does not restate, and pyqtgraph's axis text. Sizes computed from font metrics are already scaled once by the font and are scaled again by the setter -- the one way the layer can over-shrink. The main window's own size is left alone, so the gained room goes to the content.
records.translation: Stærðir sem fara ekki í gegnum setjara eru ekki endurkvarðaðar jafnóðum: texti og form sem viðmótshluti málar sjálfur í föstum pixlahnitum, pixlakort sem viðmótshluti kvarðar í tölu sem hann reiknaði, ``setFont`` með tilgreindri stærð, staðsetningar ``move``/``setGeometry``, stærðir hausahluta, Python ``sizeHint`` yfirskrift sem skilar fasta, eigin mál Fusion-stílsins sem þemablaðið endurtekur ekki, og ásatexti pyqtgraph. Stærðir sem eru reiknaðar út frá letursmálum eru þegar kvarðaðar einu sinni af letrinu og eru kvarðaðar aftur af setjaranum -- eina leiðin sem lagið getur minnkað of mikið. Eigin stærð aðalgluggans er látin í friði, svo rýmið sem vinnst fer til innihaldsins.

records.context: Templates are stored instead of finished strings. ``subtitle`` and ``description`` are what the search matches on, so they stay English: the query and the haystack must be in one language, and the index is built once per session while the interface language can change afterwards. The text shown to the user is rendered from the template when a row is drawn, by :func:`rendered_subtitle` and :func:`rendered_description` with :func:`spacr.qt.i18n.tr` passed in, so a language change takes effect at the next keystroke and this module imports neither Qt nor a catalog. "API reference" is the subtitle of about ten thousand rows; storing it as a finished English string would show those rows in English in every interface language.

records.context: The ratio belongs to the application view, not the application, and a window can be dragged from a retina laptop onto an ordinary external monitor. A picture rendered at 2x and moved to a 1x application view is merely wasteful; the reverse is blurry. :func:`follow_device_ratio` subscribes a widget to the change Qt already sends, for the pictures whose source is still in memory and whose re-render is a single call. Pictures scaled inside ``paintEvent`` need nothing: they ask for the ratio again on the next frame.

records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The ratio belongs to the screen, not the application, and a window can be dragged from a retina laptop onto an ordinary external monitor. A picture rendered at 2x and moved to a 1x screen is merely wasteful; the reverse is blurry. :func:`follow_device_ratio` subscribes a widget to the change Qt already sends, for the pictures whose source is still in memory and whose re-render is a single call. Pictures scaled inside ``paintEvent`` need nothing: they ask for the ratio again on the next frame.
records.translation: Hlutfallið tilheyrir skjánum, ekki forritinu, og glugga má draga af retina-fartölvu yfir á venjulegan ytri skjá. Mynd sem er teiknuð við 2x og færð á 1x skjá er aðeins sóun; hið gagnstæða er óskýrt. :func:`follow_device_ratio` skráir viðmótshluta í áskrift að breytingunni sem Qt sendir þegar, fyrir myndir þar sem uppsprettan er enn í minni og endurteikning er eitt kall. Myndir sem eru kvarðaðar inni í ``paintEvent`` þurfa ekkert: þær spyrja aftur um hlutfallið í næsta ramma.

records.context: ``QPixmap.scaled(w, h, ...)`` takes DEVICE pixels but every caller in a GUI means LOGICAL ones -- the size the picture should occupy on application view. On a display with a device pixel ratio of 2, which is every retina Mac and plenty of Windows and Linux machines, Qt then stretches that logical bitmap across twice as many real pixels in each direction: a 200 px render blown up to 400 px, from a 3334 px source. The picture is not low-resolution; the scaling threw the resolution away.
records.label: spacr.qt.hidpi#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: ``QPixmap.scaled(w, h, ...)`` takes DEVICE pixels but every caller in a GUI means LOGICAL ones -- the size the picture should occupy on screen. On a display with a device pixel ratio of 2, which is every retina Mac and plenty of Windows and Linux machines, Qt then stretches that logical bitmap across twice as many real pixels in each direction: a 200 px render blown up to 400 px, from a 3334 px source. The picture is not low-resolution; the scaling threw the resolution away.
records.translation: ``QPixmap.scaled(w, h, ...)`` tekur TÆKJApixla en allir sem kalla á það í GUI meina RÖKRÆNA pixla -- stærðina sem myndin á að taka á skjánum. Á skjá með tækjapixlahlutfall 2, sem á við um alla retina Mac og fjölmargar Windows- og Linux-vélar, teygir Qt þá þessa rökrænu bitamynd yfir tvöfalt fleiri raunpixla í hvora átt: 200 px teiknun blásin upp í 400 px, úr 3334 px uppsprettu. Myndin er ekki í lágri upplausn; kvörðunin henti upplausninni.

records.context: What is not live, and why that was accepted. Every size the font scale pins from Python -- row heights, column widths, icon sizes, tile geometry, all of :func:`spacr.qt.preferences.scaled_px` -- moves only when the stylesheet is rebuilt, and that is the 587 ms number. The choice made: "Text live, spacing on release." Text follows the wheel; the spacing around it catches up in one step when the wheel stops or Z comes up. It is a deliberate compromise, not an oversight, and it is why the settle exists.

records.label: spacr.qt.maturity.apply#1

records.source: Two phases:
records.translation: Tveir áfangar:

records.context: 1. :data:`PROMOTIONS` lists applications that were assessed and moved. Applying it repeatedly is safe, and it never *moves an application to a lower stage*. If another component promoted an application further, it stays there. This table represents one assessment; loading it later must not undo a newer assessment. 2. Each registered application absent from all assessment tables and without its own line receives :data:`UNASSESSED_STAGE`. This prevents a new module from inheriting ``stable`` merely because no entry exists. The function writes only empty entries, so it cannot override an author, a plugin, or step 1.
records.label: spacr.qt.maturity.apply#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: 1. :data:`PROMOTIONS` — the apps somebody assessed and moved. Idempotent, and it never *demotes*: a module some other code has already promoted further than this table says stays where it is. That matters because the table is a snapshot of one assessment, and the next assessment should not be silently undone by re-importing this module. 2. Every registered app that is in none of the assessment tables and has no line of its own is written in as :data:`UNASSESSED_STAGE`. This is what stops a new module inheriting ``stable`` from the absence of an entry — see the module docstring. It only ever writes where there is nothing, so it cannot overrule an author, a plugin, or phase 1.
records.translation: 1. :data:`PROMOTIONS` — forritin sem einhver mat og færði. Sjálfsjafnt, og það *lækkar* aldrei: eining sem annar kóði hefur þegar hækkað meira en þessi tafla segir helst þar sem hún er. Það skiptir máli því taflan er skyndimynd af einu mati, og næsta mat á ekki að afturkallast í kyrrþey við endurinnflutning þessarar einingar. 2. Hvert skráð forrit sem er í engri matstöflunni og hefur enga eigin línu er skrifað inn sem :data:`UNASSESSED_STAGE`. Þetta er það sem kemur í veg fyrir að ný eining erfi ``stable`` vegna þess að færslu vantar — sjá lýsingarstreng einingarinnar. Það skrifar aðeins þar sem ekkert er, svo það getur ekki gengið framar höfundi, viðbót eða áfanga 1.

records.context: The OPS sample is the well's last two sites because the engine takes a well's microscope field of view count as its highest site number plus one and fits the round well to that count, so a sample has to include the last site to keep the measured 333-microscope field of view layout; see :func:`spacr.ops_engine.run_ops`. And it carries no phenotype images, because the phenotype phase aligns anchors spread over the whole well, which a two-microscope field of view sample cannot supply.

records.source: The OPS sample is the well's last two sites because the engine takes a well's field count as its highest site number plus one and fits the round well to that count, so a sample has to include the last site to keep the measured 333-field layout; see :func:`spacr.ops_engine.run_ops`. And it carries no phenotype images, because the phenotype phase aligns anchors spread over the whole well, which a two-field sample cannot supply.
records.translation: OPS-sýnið eru tveir síðustu myndatökustaðir brunnsins því vélin tekur fjölda sjónsviða brunns sem hæsta staðarnúmer hans að viðbættum einum og aðlagar hringlaga brunninn að þeim fjölda, svo sýni þarf að innihalda síðasta staðinn til að halda mældu 333 sjónsviða skipulaginu; sjá :func:`spacr.ops_engine.run_ops`. Og það ber engar svipgerðarmyndir, því svipgerðaráfanginn samstillir festipunkta sem dreifast yfir allan brunninn, sem sýni með tveimur sjónsviðum getur ekki lagt til.

records.context: `spacr/qt/widgets/file_list.py` asked `os.path.exists` for every remembered path, on the main GUI execution path, to colour the missing ones red. records.source: `spacr/qt/widgets/file_list.py` asked `os.path.exists` for every remembered path, on the GUI thread, to colour the missing ones red. That is free for a local disk and it is not free for a network one: measured on one workstation, ``os.path.exists`` on a path under ``/nas_mnt`` -- an ``autofs`` mount with ``timeout=600`` -- had not returned after twenty seconds, because the stat is what triggers the automount and the share was asleep.
records.translation: `spacr/qt/widgets/file_list.py` spurði `os.path.exists` um hverja geymda slóð, á GUI-þræðinum, til að lita þær sem vantar rauðar. records.context: A registry row does not require importing its application view. :mod:`spacr.qt.app_catalog` declares the structured-data name, the name, the sentence, the section, the stage and the name of the application view factory, and :func:`spacr.qt.app_catalog.register_declared` registers all of that without importing anything; the application view is imported the first time somebody opens it. A screen that contributes a stylesheet block registers it at that import, and ``MainWindow`` applies missing registered blocks to the new screen's own QSS scope before inserting it into the visible stack. :data:`spacr.qt.theme.WIDGET_QSS_MODULES` remains the inventory used when an exhaustive/static stylesheet is explicitly requested.
records.translation: Lína í skránni krefst ekki innflutnings á skjá hennar. :mod:`spacr.qt.app_catalog` lýsir lyklinum, heitinu, setningunni, hlutanum, stiginu og heiti skjásmiðjunnar, og :func:`spacr.qt.app_catalog.register_declared` skráir allt það án þess að flytja neitt inn; skjárinn er fluttur inn í fyrsta sinn sem einhver opnar hann. Skjár sem leggur til stílblaðsblokk skráir hana við þann innflutning, og ``MainWindow`` beitir skráðum blokkum sem vantar á eigið QSS-svið nýja skjásins áður en hann er settur í sýnilega staflann. :data:`spacr.qt.theme.WIDGET_QSS_MODULES` er áfram skráin sem notuð er þegar beðið er sérstaklega um tæmandi/kyrrstætt stílblað.

records.context: **Qt Multimedia is touched only on the main GUI execution path.** :class:`_SoundPlayer` owns ``QMediaDevices`` and every ``QSoundEffect`` and lives where the application's event loop does; the dedicated ``QThread`` keeps the part that is genuinely slow, which is synthesizing a sound set (:class:`_SoundRenderer`, numpy and file writes, nothing from Qt Multimedia). Connecting to the sound server is slow -- 354 ms measured on a PipeWire workstation -- so it is made once, on an idle timer after sound is switched on (:meth:`SoundEngine._warm`), and its duration is logged. Playing an already loaded sound is ``play()``, which returns at once: 0.007-0.014 ms on the main GUI execution path against the real stack.
records.label: spacr.qt.sound#4
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Qt Multimedia is touched only on the GUI thread.** :class:`_SoundPlayer` owns ``QMediaDevices`` and every ``QSoundEffect`` and lives where the application's event loop does; the dedicated ``QThread`` keeps the part that is genuinely slow, which is synthesizing a sound set (:class:`_SoundRenderer`, numpy and file writes, nothing from Qt Multimedia). Connecting to the sound server is slow -- 354 ms measured on a PipeWire workstation -- so it is made once, on an idle timer after sound is switched on (:meth:`SoundEngine._warm`), and its duration is logged. Playing an already loaded sound is ``play()``, which returns at once: 0.007-0.014 ms on the GUI thread against the real stack.
records.translation: **Qt Multimedia er aðeins snert á GUI-þræðinum.** :class:`_SoundPlayer` á ``QMediaDevices`` og hvert ``QSoundEffect`` og er þar sem atburðalykkja forritsins er; sérstaki ``QThread`` geymir þann hluta sem er í raun hægur, sem er að búa til hljóðsafn (:class:`_SoundRenderer`, numpy og skráarskrif, ekkert úr Qt Multimedia). Tenging við hljóðþjóninn er hæg -- 354 ms mælt á PipeWire-vinnustöð -- svo hún er gerð einu sinni, á biðteljara eftir að kveikt er á hljóði (:meth:`SoundEngine._warm`), og tímalengd hennar er skráð. Spilun hljóðs sem þegar er hlaðið er ``play()``, sem skilar strax: 0.007-0.014 ms á GUI-þræðinum gagnvart raunverulega staflanum.

records.context: The rule follows from a crash. Building the effects on the audio independent execution path instead does move the connection off the main GUI execution path -- but Qt Multimedia's device handling belongs to the independent execution path that owns the event loop, so with the FFmpeg backend it enables socket notifiers from the wrong independent execution path. Reopening Preferences with sound on then segfaults, or wedges the interface with an empty Preferences frame until it is force quit.

records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The rule follows from a crash. Building the effects on the audio thread instead does move the connection off the GUI thread -- but Qt Multimedia's device handling belongs to the thread that owns the event loop, so with the FFmpeg backend it enables socket notifiers from the wrong thread. Reopening Preferences with sound on then segfaults, or wedges the interface with an empty Preferences frame until it is force quit.
records.translation: Reglan leiðir af hruni. Ef áhrifin eru byggð á hljóðþræðinum í staðinn færist tengingin vissulega af GUI-þræðinum -- en tækjameðhöndlun Qt Multimedia tilheyrir þræðinum sem á atburðalykkjuna, svo með FFmpeg-bakendanum virkjar hún sökkultilkynningar frá röngum þræði. Ef Preferences er síðan opnað aftur með kveikt á hljóði verður segfault, eða viðmótið festist með tómum Preferences-ramma þar til það er þvingað til að hætta.

records.context: A flood fill from one click is the fastest way to take a whole object, and it has one failure mode that matters: the object touches something bright that is not it -- a debris streak, a saturated membrane seam, the rim of a well -- and the flood walks out along that seam and swallows the microscope field of view. The tolerance that takes the object correctly and the tolerance that escapes are often the same number, so "lower the tolerance" is not an answer: it shrinks the object as well.

The tolerance that takes the object correctly and the tolerance that escapes are often the same number, so "lower the tolerance" is not an answer: it shrinks the object as well.
records.translation: Flæðifylling frá einum smelli er fljótlegasta leiðin til að taka heilan hlut, og hún hefur eina bilunarleið sem skiptir máli: hluturinn snertir eitthvað bjart sem er ekki hann -- rusláka, mettaða himnusamskeyti, brún brunns -- og flæðið gengur út eftir þeim samskeytum og gleypir sjónsviðið. Vikmörkin sem taka hlutinn rétt og vikmörkin sem sleppa út eru oft sama talan, svo "lower the tolerance" (lækka vikmörkin) er ekki svar: það minnkar hlutinn líka.

records.context: 1. **Directional runaway detection and trimming** — :func:`trim_directional_runaway` measures flood width along scanlines extending from the seed. A sustained abrupt expansion marks a leak, and pixels beyond that position are removed. Detection at this stage enables the following two refinements. 2. **Intensity-constrained reflooding** — :func:`wand_region` performs a binary search for the highest tested tolerance that does not trigger runaway detection. The resulting connected region replaces the straight-line directional cut. 3. **Gradient-based boundary refinement** — :func:`taper_region_to_intensity` applies a watershed to a smoothed intensity gradient within a configurable band, moving the provisional boundary toward a nearby image edge.
records.label: spacr.qt.wand_rescue#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: 1. **Directional runaway detection and trimming** — :func:`trim_directional_runaway` measures flood width along scanlines extending from the seed. A sustained abrupt expansion marks a leak, and pixels beyond that position are removed. Detection at this stage enables the following two refinements. 2. **Intensity-constrained reflooding** — :func:`wand_region` performs a binary search for the highest tested tolerance that does not trigger runaway detection. The resulting connected region replaces the straight-line directional cut. 3. **Gradient-based boundary refinement** — :func:`taper_region_to_intensity` applies a watershed to a smoothed intensity gradient within a configurable band, moving the provisional boundary toward a nearby image edge.
records.translation: 1. **Greining og snyrting á stefnubundnu útflæði** — :func:`trim_directional_runaway` mælir breidd flæðisins eftir skannlínum sem liggja út frá fræpunktinum. Viðvarandi skyndileg útvíkkun markar leka, og pixlar handan þeirrar staðsetningar eru fjarlægðir. Greining á þessu stigi gerir tvær næstu fínstillingar mögulegar. 2. **Endurflæði takmarkað af birtu** — :func:`wand_region` framkvæmir helmingunarleit að hæstu prófuðu vikmörkum sem kalla ekki fram útflæðisgreiningu. Samtengda svæðið sem af hlýst kemur í stað beina stefnuskurðarins. 3. **Fínstilling marka byggð á stigli** — :func:`taper_region_to_intensity` beitir vatnaskilum á jafnaðan birtustigul innan stillanlegs bands og færir bráðabirgðamörkin í átt að nálægri brún í myndinni.

records.context: The masthead builds this label with ``setSizePolicy(QSizePolicy.Maximum, ...)`` and ``setMinimumWidth(0)`` and documents the intent -- the blurb "may shrink below its ideal width rather than force the window wider". Neither call achieves it: ``qSmartMinSize`` takes a shrinkable widget's minimum from ``minimumSizeHint()``, which for a non-wrapping ``QLabel`` is the width of the entire sentence, and it only lets an explicit ``minimumWidth`` override that when the value is greater than zero. Without this override the blurb, the one masthead control that can lose text harmlessly, gave up no width.

Neither call achieves it: ``qSmartMinSize`` takes a shrinkable widget's minimum from ``minimumSizeHint()``, which for a non-wrapping ``QLabel`` is the width of the entire sentence, and it only lets an explicit ``minimumWidth`` override that when the value is greater than zero. records.context: A view is one visit to one application view: it begins when the application view is shown (:meth:`begin_view`, from its ``showEvent``) and ends when it is hidden because the user went to another application view (:meth:`end_view`, from its ``hideEvent``). Minimising the window does not end it -- the owner passes only non-spontaneous events. Pins last for the view: returning to the application view with its live preview still open collapses the surroundings again, which is what a fresh arrival at that layout would get.

Minimising the window does not end it -- the owner passes only non-spontaneous events. records.translation: Sýn er ein heimsókn á einn skjá: hún hefst þegar skjárinn er sýndur (:meth:`begin_view`, úr ``showEvent`` hans) og lýkur þegar hann er falinn vegna þess að notandinn fór á annan skjá (:meth:`end_view`, úr ``hideEvent`` hans). Lágmörkun gluggans lýkur henni ekki -- eigandinn sendir aðeins atburði sem eru ekki sjálfsprottnir. Festingar vara út sýnina: þegar snúið er aftur á skjáinn með lifandi forskoðun hans enn opna fellist umhverfið aftur saman, sem er það sem ný koma að því útliti myndi fá.

records.context: The body's own visibility stays under its owner's control. The fold hides an inner holder, never the body, so unfolding cannot show a panel its owner hid or build a panel that is built on first show. The other way round, the section follows its body: while the owner keeps the body hidden the whole section -- heading included -- is hidden too, and it comes back when the owner shows the body. Only the body's hidden flag is read for that, so nothing is shown, measured or built to find out.

records.context: Lifted out of `spacr.qt.screens.settings_model`, where it was written for the settings panel's chip strip, because a wrapping row is not a settings idea: the regression results header wants one too. Three combo boxes with minimum widths, a processing session name of unpredictable length and a QHBoxLayout do not fit in a narrow panel, and Qt's answer to a box it cannot satisfy is to let the children overlap -- measured at 577 px, where the second box started 48 px inside the first and the third ran 32 px off the panel.

records.source: Lifted out of `spacr.qt.screens.settings_model`, where it was written for the settings panel's chip strip, because a wrapping row is not a settings idea: the regression results header wants one too. Three combo boxes with minimum widths, a run name of unpredictable length and a QHBoxLayout do not fit in a narrow panel, and Qt's answer to a box it cannot satisfy is to let the children overlap -- measured at 577 px, where the second box started 48 px inside the first and the third ran 32 px off the panel.
records.translation: Tekið úr `spacr.qt.screens.settings_model`, þar sem það var skrifað fyrir merkjastiku stillingaspjaldsins, því röð sem brýtur línur er ekki stillingahugmynd: haus aðhvarfsniðurstaðnanna vill líka slíka. Þrír fellilistar með lágmarksbreidd, keyrsluheiti af ófyrirsjáanlegri lengd og QHBoxLayout komast ekki fyrir í mjóu spjaldi, og svar Qt við reit sem það getur ekki uppfyllt er að láta börnin skarast -- mælt við 577 px, þar sem annar reiturinn byrjaði 48 px inni í þeim fyrsta og sá þriðji náði 32 px út fyrir spjaldið.

records.context: Why it is a second entry rather than a backend switch. The CPU path jitters four samples ACROSS four frames, which averages four different animation times; a GPU pass can afford the four samples inside one instant. They are not the same picture, so offering them as one option with a hidden backend would mean the same setting drawing two things. "Orbit fold" is taken, so this is "Orbit fold (sharp)" -- descriptive of what actually differs rather than a version number.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.fractal_orbit_gpu#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: WHY IT IS A SECOND ENTRY RATHER THAN A BACKEND SWITCH. The CPU path jitters four samples ACROSS four frames, which averages four different animation times; a GPU pass can afford the four samples inside one instant. They are not the same picture, so offering them as one option with a hidden backend would mean the same setting drawing two things. "Orbit fold" is taken, so this is "Orbit fold (sharp)" -- descriptive of what actually differs rather than a version number.
records.translation: HVERS VEGNA ÞETTA ER ÖNNUR FÆRSLA FREMUR EN BAKENDAROFI. CPU-leiðin hnikar fjórum úrtökum YFIR fjóra ramma, sem tekur meðaltal af fjórum ólíkum hreyfitímum; GPU-umferð hefur efni á fjórum úrtökum innan eins augnabliks. Þetta er ekki sama myndin, svo ef þau væru boðin sem einn valkostur með földum bakenda myndi sama stilling teikna tvennt. "Orbit fold" er þegar notað, svo þetta er "Orbit fold (sharp)" -- lýsandi fyrir það sem raunverulega er ólíkt fremur en útgáfunúmer.

records.context: ``General`` How much data is loaded and how the cloud is drawn. The settings are here; the workspace they drive is the next piece of work.
records.translation: ``General`` Hve mikið af gögnum er hlaðið og hvernig punktaskýið er teiknað. records.context: Layers are composited with the "over" operator, bottom first. The canvas starts black. Each ticked layer, bottom first, is laid on with its opacity ``a``: where it covers, ``out = out * (1 - a) + colour * a``; where it does not, ``out`` is left alone. An image covers every pixel; a mask covers its objects only, so the background of a mask never dims what is under it. The result is rounded to the nearest whole grey level.

records.source: Layers are composited with the "over" operator, bottom first. The canvas starts black. An image covers every pixel; a mask covers its objects only, so the background of a mask never dims what is under it. The result is rounded to the nearest whole grey level.
records.translation: Lög eru samsett með "over" aðgerðinni, neðsta fyrst. Striginn byrjar svartur. Hvert lag sem hakað er við, neðsta fyrst, er lagt á með ógegnsæi sínu ``a``: þar sem það þekur er ``out = out * (1 - a) + colour * a``; þar sem það þekur ekki er ``out`` látið óhreyft. Mynd þekur hvern pixil; gríma þekur aðeins hluti sína, svo bakgrunnur grímu deyfir aldrei það sem er undir henni. Útkoman er námunduð að næsta heila gráskalagildi.

records.context: The grid in :mod:`spacr.qt.widgets.object_settings_grid` edits values; the settings panel is a key-value mapping of widgets, and the workflow reads the widgets. Mounting the grid without a binding would give an application view two answers to the same question -- the table showing what the user typed and ``collect()`` still returning what the widget holds -- and the processing session would silently use the second one, so the saved settings would differ from what the grid shows.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.object_grid_binding#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The grid in :mod:`spacr.qt.widgets.object_settings_grid` edits values; the settings panel is a dictionary of widgets, and the pipeline reads the widgets. Mounting the grid without a binding would give a screen two answers to the same question -- the table showing what the user typed and ``collect()`` still returning what the widget holds -- and the run would silently use the second one, so the saved settings would differ from what the grid shows.
records.translation: Hnitanetið í :mod:`spacr.qt.widgets.object_settings_grid` breytir gildum; stillingaspjaldið er orðabók viðmótshluta, og vinnslulínan les viðmótshlutana. Ef hnitanetið væri sett upp án bindingar fengi skjár tvö svör við sömu spurningu -- taflan sýndi það sem notandinn sló inn og ``collect()`` skilaði enn því sem viðmótshlutinn geymir -- og keyrslan myndi í kyrrþey nota seinna svarið, svo vistuðu stillingarnar yrðu aðrar en það sem hnitanetið sýnir.

records.context: So the grid never becomes the source of truth. It is a view that writes through: every edit lands in the widget behind it, and the widget stays what the workflow reads. Nothing downstream of ``collect()`` learns that the grid exists, so no settings file, notebook or ``spacr-run`` invocation changes.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.object_grid_binding#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context

records.translation: Hnitanetið verður því aldrei sannleiksuppsprettan. records.context: Windows opened from the preview are not scaled with it. A dialog parented to the panel is a window of its own, yet Qt cascades the panel's scaled sheet into it, and the walk found it among the panel's children: at 150 % a settings dialog's buttons were 59 px tall, not the 40 px of every other dialog. Such a window and everything in it are kept at 100 %, and the window's own sheet re-states, at 100 %, the sizes it would otherwise inherit scaled -- set as it is polished, so before it is first laid out.

Gluggi sem hefur spjaldið sem foreldri er sjálfstæður gluggi, en Qt lætur kvarðað stílblað spjaldsins flæða inn í hann, og yfirferðin fann hann meðal barna spjaldsins: við 150 % voru hnappar stillingaglugga 59 px háir, ekki 40 px eins og í öllum öðrum gluggum. Slíkur gluggi og allt í honum er haldið við 100 %, og eigið stílblað gluggans endurtekur, við 100 %, stærðirnar sem hann myndi annars erfa kvarðaðar -- stillt um leið og hann er fágaður, svo áður en honum er fyrst raðað upp.

records.context: An owner can replace renderers. The default renderers draw a plain overlay, categorical masks, the flows as Cellpose hands them and the probability on the magma scale. An owner with its own idea of an outline -- the live preview's colour choice and thickness -- registers a renderer for that view with :meth:`SegmentationViews.set_renderer` and keeps the other three. A renderer answers with a picture, with a sentence to show in the picture's place, or with ``None`` for the widget's own "nothing yet" sentence.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.segmentation_views#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: An owner can replace renderers. The default renderers draw a plain overlay, categorical masks, the flows as Cellpose hands them and the probability on the magma scale. An owner with its own idea of an outline -- the live preview's colour choice and thickness -- registers a renderer for that view with :meth:`SegmentationViews.set_renderer` and keeps the other three. A renderer answers with a picture, with a sentence to show in the picture's place, or with ``None`` for the widget's own "nothing yet" sentence.
records.translation: Eigandi getur skipt út teiknurum. Sjálfgefnu teiknararnir teikna einfalt yfirlag, flokkagrímur, flæðin eins og Cellpose afhendir þau og líkurnar á magma-kvarðanum. Eigandi með eigin hugmynd um útlínu -- litaval og þykkt lifandi forskoðunarinnar -- skráir teiknara fyrir þá sýn með :meth:`SegmentationViews.set_renderer` og heldur hinum þremur. Teiknari svarar með mynd, með setningu til að sýna í stað myndarinnar, eða með ``None`` fyrir eigin "nothing yet" (ekkert enn) setningu viðmótshlutans.

records.context: The canvas is pluggable. An owner that already has a canvas with a ruler and a hover line on it (the live preview's ``_ZoomView``) hands it in; otherwise a :class:`PictureCanvas` is built, which fits, zooms, pans and saves on a right click like every other picture in the program.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.segmentation_views#4
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The canvas is pluggable. An owner that already has a canvas with a ruler and a hover line on it (the live preview's ``_ZoomView``) hands it in; otherwise a :class:`PictureCanvas` is built, which fits, zooms, pans and saves on a right click like every other picture in the program.
records.translation: Hægt er að skipta um striga. Eigandi sem hefur þegar striga með reglustiku og sveimilínu (``_ZoomView`` lifandi forskoðunarinnar) afhendir hann; annars er byggður :class:`PictureCanvas`, sem aðlagast, þysjar, hliðrast og vistar við hægrismell eins og allar aðrar myndir í forritinu.

records.context: What this module adds is the tie. Two views of the same region are only worth putting side by side if they stay in register: a curator comparing a field with its enhanced self is looking for a difference between them, and a difference in where the two are pointing is the one difference that is not information. :meth:`ZoomableImageView.link_to` makes a group of views share one zoom and one scroll position, so zooming or panning any of them moves all of them.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.zoom_view#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: What this module adds is the tie. Two views of the same region are only worth putting side by side if they stay in register: a curator comparing a field with its enhanced self is looking for a difference between them, and a difference in where the two are pointing is the one difference that is not information. :meth:`ZoomableImageView.link_to` makes a group of views share one zoom and one scroll position, so zooming or panning any of them moves all of them.
records.translation: Það sem þessi eining bætir við er tengingin. Tvær sýnir af sama svæði eru aðeins þess virði að setja hlið við hlið ef þær haldast samstilltar: sá sem flokkar myndir og ber sjónsvið saman við bætta útgáfu þess leitar að mun á þeim, og munur á því hvert þær tvær beinast er eini munurinn sem felur ekki í sér upplýsingar. :meth:`ZoomableImageView.link_to` lætur hóp sýna deila einum aðdrætti og einni skrunstöðu, svo aðdráttur eða hliðrun á einhverri þeirra færir þær allar.
